title: Unresolved: Alleged Firing of Three Sentencing Commission Members
description_short: Unresolved: Alleged Firing of Three Sentencing Commission Members
description_medium: The supplied U.S. Sentencing Commission press-release archive contains general agency material, not a notice that Trump removed three commissioners on January 20, 2025. The packet does not name the members or supply dismissal letters, contemporaneous reporting, a case filing, or the legal text said to require cause. The alleged event and legal dispute are therefore unverified; exclude pending names and case-specific documentation.
description_long: The linked source is the U.S. Sentencing Commission’s general press-release archive. It describes the Commission but does not document the alleged removal of three members on January 20, 2025. The assignment packet does not identify the three people, their terms or appointment status, any communication from the White House, or a contemporaneous report of their removal. It also claims the removals were legally contested because the statute required cause, but provides no statute section, court filing, statement from an affected commissioner, or case status. Without those details, the record cannot distinguish a firing from a request to resign, another commission’s personnel change, or an incorrect date. The proper proposal is to hold the allegation out of the chronology until the people and action can be verified with a removal notice or reliable event-specific reporting; the legal characterization separately requires statutory and litigation support. The archive alone supports institutional background, not this event.

supported_facts: The Commission chair’s January 24, 2025 remarks state that Judges Claria Horn Boom and John Gleeson’s service ended earlier that month.
limitations: The remarks do not say President Trump removed the judges; the prior source review identifies two earlier service endings, not three January 20 removals.

supported_facts: The official page is a January 24, 2025 U.S. Sentencing Commission news release seeking comment on proposed amendments.
limitations: It does not identify three commissioners removed by Trump on January 20 or document a related legal challenge.

supported_facts: 28 U.S.C. § 991(a) says a Commission member may be removed only for neglect of duty, malfeasance, or other good cause.
limitations: The statute establishes the legal standard but does not establish that a removal occurred or that litigation challenged one.

supported_facts: The supplied official URL is the U.S. Sentencing Commission’s general press-release archive.
limitations: The inspected archive page provides general agency and press-release material, not an event-specific notice identifying the alleged three removals.
